groups.name: wow
groups.description: The host's configuration, the `wow.*` namespace: the node, its internal port, its stores and logs, the cluster, the commands' waits and execution, the subscriptions, the timers and schedules, the HTTP edge and the calls to other contexts. No key keeps a 9.x meaning; the defaults are the runtime's own. The query plane, Kafka, ClickHouse and OpenTelemetry have their own classes (QueryProperties, KafkaProperties, ClickHouseProperties, ObservabilityProperties). Every key is in the host's configuration metadata (`META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json`), and a `wow.*` key that no property of the host or of a module names is reported at startup (ConfigurationKeys).

groups.name: wow.calls
groups.description: The synchronous calls of the node's sagas to the command gateways of other contexts. A saga that calls a context without a URL fails, then parks.

groups.name: wow.clickhouse
groups.description: ClickHouse's configuration, `wow.clickhouse.*`, read when wow-clickhouse is on the classpath (ClickHouseAutoConfiguration): the server, the Sink that writes the published streams, and the dataset queries.

groups.name: wow.clickhouse.query
groups.description: The datasets served from ClickHouse.

groups.name: wow.clickhouse.sink
groups.description: The Sink that writes the Manifest's published streams to ClickHouse.

groups.name: wow.clients
groups.description: The typed clients of the peer contexts over HTTP, `wow-client`'s: a peer context listed in contexts is reached over HTTP by the service's me.ahoo.wow.api.client.CommandClient and me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi beans; any other context as without these clients (its commands through its topic). An application's me.ahoo.wow.client.EndpointResolver bean may resolve where each peer is instead. The service mode presents the me.ahoo.wow.api.client.ServiceCredential bean (`wow.calls.token`).

groups.name: wow.clients.retry
groups.description: How a request a peer answered with a problem a retry may get past is sent again.

groups.name: wow.cluster
groups.description: How the nodes of a service share the partitions of each context's log, and forward commands to their owners.

groups.name: wow.contexts
groups.description: The bounded contexts the node serves.

groups.name: wow.cosec
groups.description: The keys wow-cosec reads (`wow.cosec.*`), bound here so they are checked and documented as the others are.

groups.name: wow.cosec.authorizer
groups.description: CoSec's authorization of the commands.

groups.name: wow.cosec.cross-scope
groups.description: The callers that may act across scopes: by CoSec role or policy.

groups.name: wow.cosec.service
groups.description: The service identities, whose synchronous calls the internal port takes.

groups.name: wow.cosec.tenant-level
groups.description: The tenant-level callers, who read and write every aggregate of their tenant.

groups.name: wow.cosid
groups.description: The keys wow-cosid reads (`wow.cosid.*`), bound here as cosec is.

groups.name: wow.executor
groups.description: How the node executes commands.

groups.name: wow.health
groups.description: The node's health and its probes, when the application has Spring Boot Actuator: `wow.health.*`.

groups.name: wow.health.executor
groups.description: The node's command executors.

groups.name: wow.health.liveness
groups.description: Whether the node is stuck, so a restart helps; a storage outage never fails it.

groups.name: wow.health.ownership
groups.description: The node's share of each lease group's partitions.

groups.name: wow.health.stores
groups.description: The node's event logs, as its own calls and a probe of their heads see them.

groups.name: wow.health.subscriptions
groups.description: The node's subscriptions, never a reason to take it out of service.

groups.name: wow.health.topics
groups.description: The topics of other contexts the node reads.

groups.name: wow.http
groups.description: The HTTP edge: its routes, its error answers and the services the internal port trusts.

groups.name: wow.http.manifest
groups.description: The service's Manifest route.

groups.name: wow.http.openapi
groups.description: The OpenAPI document of the routes.

groups.name: wow.http.openapi.springdoc
groups.description: The springdoc bridge, when the application has springdoc.

groups.name: wow.internal
groups.description: The internal port: the cluster channel, the wait signals and the calls of other services.

groups.name: wow.kafka
groups.description: The Kafka transport's configuration, `wow.kafka.*`: the brokers, the clients' settings and the topics, which the transport provider of type `kafka` reads (`me.ahoo.wow.kafka.KafkaTransportProvider`, finding R5.B-5), and the topic prefix, the command intake and the topics' DDL and partition refresh, which the node reads whatever transport carries them (TransportAutoConfiguration). The keys stay until the configuration surface is final.

groups.name: wow.kafka.topics
groups.description: The topics the node's contexts own, and how `auto` creates them.

groups.name: wow.log
groups.description: The aggregates' logs: their partitions, their store, and how their appends and tails run.

groups.name: wow.log.append-queue
groups.description: How the appends of one partition are queued and grouped into one call: `wow.log.append-queue.*`.

groups.name: wow.log.handoff
groups.description: The hand-over of the node's own commits to its tails in memory: a tail waits its gap wait for a missing sequence and maxPollInterval without a commit before it reads the store.

groups.name: wow.mongo
groups.description: The defaults of the MongoDB stores.

groups.name: wow.node
groups.description: This node's identity among the nodes of the service, and where they reach it.

groups.name: wow.opentelemetry
groups.description: Observability's configuration, `wow.opentelemetry.*`, read when wow-opentelemetry is on the classpath (ObservabilityAutoConfiguration).

groups.name: wow.ops
groups.description: The operator's side of the parked entries: their routes, the webhook told when an entry parks, and the failure ledger published to the ops context.

groups.name: wow.ops.publish
groups.description: Publishing the failure ledger to the ops context.

groups.name: wow.ops.webhook
groups.description: The webhook told when an entry parks or spends its retries.

groups.name: wow.postgres
groups.description: The defaults of the PostgreSQL stores.

groups.name: wow.query
groups.description: The query plane's configuration, `wow.query.*`, read by QueryAutoConfiguration: the query routes and gateways, the budgets they run under, who may query what, and how many queries each store runs at once.

groups.name: wow.query.abac
groups.description: Attribute-based access control of the queries: the caller's tags matched against the snapshots' `tags`.

groups.name: wow.query.adaptive
groups.description: How the bound of a store adapts to its write pressure, when neither `wow.query.max-concurrent` nor `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-concurrent` fixes it.

groups.name: wow.query.count-cache
groups.description: The cache of the snapshot counts.

groups.name: wow.query.cross-tenant
groups.description: Queries across tenants on the query routes.

groups.name: wow.query.dataset
groups.description: The datasets, and the bound of their queries.

groups.name: wow.query.events
groups.description: The `events` model, served from each aggregate's log store, or the store its `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.store` names.

groups.name: wow.query.http
groups.description: The budget every query route runs under (QueryBudget); a limit of `0` is off.

groups.name: wow.query.in-process
groups.description: The budget of in-process queries, the typed me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi's, trusted code's too: the same keys and defaults as `wow.query.http.*`.

groups.name: wow.query.index
groups.description: The indexes of each aggregate's `x-wow-index`.

groups.name: wow.query.memory
groups.description: Queries of the snapshots and logs kept in memory.

groups.name: wow.query.sensitivity
groups.description: What the queries may do with sensitive fields.

groups.name: wow.query.state
groups.description: The reads of an aggregate's state at a version or a point in time.

groups.name: wow.query.stream
groups.description: How a `list` streamed as server-sent events reads its chunks and how long it runs.

groups.name: wow.snapshot
groups.description: Where the snapshots are by default, and how the snapshot maintenance runs: `wow.snapshot.*`.

groups.name: wow.state-cache
groups.description: The cache of aggregate states each context keeps between commands.

groups.name: wow.state-views
groups.description: The bounds of each context's state views: `wow.state-views.*`.

groups.name: wow.subscription
groups.description: How the node's subscriptions run, retry their failures and park what keeps failing.

groups.name: wow.subscription.backpressure
groups.description: How a handler whose downstream pushes back is retried, and its partition throttled.

groups.name: wow.subscription.parked
groups.description: How the parked entries are retried automatically, over minutes and hours.

groups.name: wow.subscription.read-retry
groups.description: How a failing read of the log, or write of a store, is retried: until the node stops, the backoff growing for `max-attempts` (5) attempts, after which each failure is logged as an error and retried at `max-backoff`, so a long outage does not stop the subscription.

groups.name: wow.subscription.retry
groups.description: How a failing handler is retried in process before its aggregate is parked; a subscription's `wow.subscriptions.[<subscription>].retry.*` and its handler's `@Retry` come before it.

groups.name: wow.subscription.systemic
groups.description: When a partition pauses on a systemic failure, such as a database that is down, instead of parking every aggregate that fails.

groups.name: wow.tenant
groups.description: The tenants of the callers.

groups.name: wow.timers
groups.description: The node's firing loop of the timers, which sends the scheduled commands when they are due.

groups.name: wow.topics
groups.description: The node's topics without Kafka, for local development, see Topics.

groups.name: wow.wait
groups.description: How long and how far the commands' waits go.

properties.name: wow.aggregates
properties.description: Per aggregate type, by `<context>.<aggregate>` (bracketed in a property name: `wow.aggregates.[shop.cart]`).

properties.name: wow.backend
properties.description: The backend of a node that names no `wow.stores`: `auto` (the default) takes PostgreSQL or MongoDB by the application's `DataSource` or `MongoClient`, and refuses to start without either, so that data is not lost by mistake, unless a profile of `wow.internal.dev-profiles` is active or the internal port binds the loopback interface alone; `memory` keeps the data in memory on purpose, for one node whose data does not outlive it. `postgres`, `mongo` or the type of a community backend's store provider (`me.ahoo.wow.spi.store.StoreProvider`) name one.

properties.name: wow.calls.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long one call may take to connect.

properties.name: wow.calls.contexts
properties.description: Each context's base URL, `wow.calls.contexts.<context>.url`: the target's internal port, `http://host:port` of an address in its internal network, never its public port, which refuses calls.

properties.name: wow.calls.timeout
properties.description: How long one call may take.

properties.name: wow.calls.token
properties.description: The service token the node presents as `Authorization: Bearer`; an application's me.ahoo.wow.api.client.ServiceCredential bean, such as one that renews a CoSec token, replaces it.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.database
properties.description: The database that holds the tables.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.endpoint
properties.description: The server's HTTP endpoint, such as `http://localhost:8123`; ClickHouse is wired only when it is set.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.password
properties.description: The password to sign in with.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.query.enabled
properties.description: Whether the datasets are served from ClickHouse.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.query.metadata-ttl
properties.description: How long a dataset table's columns and engine are reused before `system.columns` is read again.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.query.settings
properties.description: Server settings every dataset query runs under, such as `max_memory_usage`; the execution time comes from each query's budget (`wow.query.http.timeout`), not from here.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.sink.aggregates
properties.description: By context, then by aggregate name.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.sink.batch-size
properties.description: The most records one insert carries.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.sink.ddl
properties.description: How the Sink manages its tables: `auto` creates what is missing, then validates; `validate` or `none`.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.sink.deduplication-window
properties.description: How many recent inserts each table remembers to drop a retried one: the `non_replicated_deduplication_window` of the tables `auto` creates.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.sink.enabled
properties.description: Whether the Manifest's published streams are written to ClickHouse.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.username
properties.description: The user name to sign in with.

properties.name: wow.clients.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long a request may take to connect.

properties.name: wow.clients.contexts
properties.description: The peer contexts reached over HTTP, by context: one the api jars on the class path declare, or one described by its Manifest alone (`contract: manifest`), called with me.ahoo.wow.client.NamedCommands.

properties.name: wow.clients.forwarded-headers
properties.description: The headers of the public request it serves that a user-mode request forwards.

properties.name: wow.clients.mode
properties.description: The mode of a peer that names none: `service`, through its internal port as this service, or `user`, through its public routes with the end user's credential.

properties.name: wow.clients.retry.backoff
properties.description: The wait before the first retry when the peer gives no `Retry-After`; it doubles at each next one.

properties.name: wow.clients.retry.max-attempts
properties.description: The most attempts of a request in all; 1 never retries.

properties.name: wow.clients.retry.max-retry-after
properties.description: The longest `Retry-After` of a peer that is waited out; a peer that asks for longer is not retried.

properties.name: wow.clients.timeout
properties.description: How long a request may take to be answered, a command's longer wait aside.

properties.name: wow.cluster.drain-timeout
properties.description: How long a hand-off of a partition waits for its commands in flight before it moves on.

properties.name: wow.cluster.forward-timeout
properties.description: How long a forward waits for the owner's reply, capped by the command's own deadline: `wow.wait.default-timeout` when not set, so a node whose waits are longer forwards as long. A forward the owner received and did not answer by then is reported unknown (`wow.command.unknown`), not run here, so the command never runs twice and a retry with the same request id is safe.

properties.name: wow.cluster.heartbeat-interval
properties.description: How often a node sends its heartbeat; less than half of `member-ttl`, so one late heartbeat is harmless.

properties.name: wow.cluster.lease-parallelism
properties.description: The most lease acquisitions a node runs at a time.

properties.name: wow.cluster.lease-ttl
properties.description: How long a partition stays with a node that stopped renewing its lease.

properties.name: wow.cluster.max-in-flight-per-peer
properties.description: The forwards one peer may have outstanding; one more runs here instead.

properties.name: wow.cluster.member-ttl
properties.description: How long a node stays a member of the cluster after its last heartbeat.

properties.name: wow.cluster.reconcile-interval
properties.description: How often a node compares the partitions it holds with those it should hold; a change of the members it notices reconciles at once.

properties.name: wow.cluster.reconcile-timeout
properties.description: How long one reconcile may run before the node takes itself as stuck and leaves the members until it ends, so the other nodes take the partitions it cannot run; longer than `drain-timeout`.

properties.name: wow.cluster.renew-interval
properties.description: How often a node renews its leases; less than half of `lease-ttl`, or every lease is lost between rounds.

properties.name: wow.cluster.route-refresh-interval
properties.description: How often the route table is read from the leases and members; a failed forward refreshes it at once.

properties.name: wow.cluster.router
properties.description: Where commands run: `partitioned`, on the owner of the aggregate's partition, or `local`, here. `local` on the memory backend, which cannot route across nodes, and `partitioned` on the others when not set.

properties.name: wow.contexts.exclude
properties.description: The contexts the node does not serve, taken out of those include gives.

properties.name: wow.contexts.include
properties.description: The contexts the node serves; every context on the class path when empty.

properties.name: wow.cosec.authorizer.enabled
properties.description: Whether CoSec authorizes every command as its caller (`CoSecCommandAuthorizer`), not only the public routes by path; the services' calls are authorized by CoSec whatever this says.

properties.name: wow.cosec.cross-scope.policies
properties.description: The CoSec policies of these callers.

properties.name: wow.cosec.cross-scope.roles
properties.description: The CoSec roles of these callers.

properties.name: wow.cosec.service.policies
properties.description: The CoSec policies of these callers.

properties.name: wow.cosec.service.roles
properties.description: The CoSec roles of these callers.

properties.name: wow.cosec.tenant-level.policies
properties.description: The CoSec policies of these callers.

properties.name: wow.cosec.tenant-level.roles
properties.description: The CoSec roles of these callers.

properties.name: wow.cosec.trust-injected-app
properties.description: Whether a service in CoSec's inject mode, behind a CoSec gateway (`cosec.inject.enabled=true` with `cosec.authorization.enabled=false`), records the application of the requests the gateway forwards, their `CoSec-App-Id`, as the caller's app and the request fact `app_id`: it trusts the gateway, so it is off by default; in any other mode it fails the startup.

properties.name: wow.cosid.global-generator
properties.description: The CosId generator of the node's global ids (command ids, wait ids); CosId's own `cosid` when not set.

properties.name: wow.ddl
properties.description: How the stores manage the framework's tables, collections and indexes: `auto` creates what is missing (the default), `validate` creates nothing and refuses a store whose schema is missing or in another format, `none` creates and checks nothing; `wow.stores.<name>.ddl` overrides it for one store.

properties.name: wow.executor.lane-capacity
properties.description: The commands one aggregate may have waiting in the executor.

properties.name: wow.executor.max-batch
properties.description: The most of one aggregate's queued commands the executor decides in turn and commits with one append; 1 runs each alone. It never waits to fill a batch.

properties.name: wow.executor.max-in-flight
properties.description: The commands the node may have in flight, all contexts together: beyond it a command is refused as `wow.command.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`) instead of queued.

properties.name: wow.health.enabled
properties.description: Whether the host contributes the node's health to Actuator and its probe groups.

properties.name: wow.health.executor.saturation
properties.description: The share of `wow.executor.max-in-flight` in flight at which the executor is degraded.

properties.name: wow.health.liveness.stall-timeout
properties.description: How long the node's dispatcher may not tick, or commands in flight not finish while every log answers, before the node is not live.

properties.name: wow.health.ownership.handover-grace
properties.description: How long the owned partitions may differ from the node's share (a hand-over) before the group is degraded, and down (the node not ready) when it owns none of a share that is not empty.

properties.name: wow.health.sample-interval
properties.description: How often the node samples what a probe must not wait for (the logs' heads, the subscriptions' lag and parked entries) and probes its stores.

properties.name: wow.health.stores.down-after
properties.description: How long a log must keep failing, with no success since, before it is down and the node not ready: a failed call or probe, or a probe that timed out (after this long, at least a second); a probe still under way is no failure. `0s` is down at the first failure.

properties.name: wow.health.stores.window
properties.description: A log with a failure this recent is degraded.

properties.name: wow.health.subscriptions.lag-degraded-at
properties.description: The entries a subscription may be behind the log's head before it is degraded.

properties.name: wow.health.subscriptions.parked-degraded-at
properties.description: The parked entries of a subscription, counted up to this, at which it is degraded (as when they grow).

properties.name: wow.health.topics.required
properties.description: Whether a topic the node is still joining makes it not ready; degraded only when false.

properties.name: wow.http.client-facts
properties.description: Whether the public port records each command's client address and `User-Agent` as the request facts `remote_ip` and `user_agent`, as 9.x did, for audit. They are personal data, and written into the event stream, which is never deleted: once recorded, they cannot be erased. On by default; off records neither.

properties.name: wow.http.errors
properties.description: The HTTP status of an error code, by code (bracketed in a property name: `wow.http.errors.[a.b].status`).

properties.name: wow.http.global-errors
properties.description: Answers what fails on the application's own routes as the framework routes' problem+json, so every route answers errors alike: on by default; off leaves those errors to Spring's error handling.

properties.name: wow.http.manifest.enabled
properties.description: Serves `GET /wow/manifest`.

properties.name: wow.http.openapi.enabled
properties.description: Serves `GET /wow/openapi`, the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the routes.

properties.name: wow.http.openapi.springdoc.enabled
properties.description: Merges the Wow routes into springdoc's documents.

properties.name: wow.http.openapi.springdoc.group
properties.description: The springdoc group of the Wow routes alone: `/v3/api-docs/<group>`.

properties.name: wow.http.request-facts
properties.description: The request headers copied into a command's headers, beside the standard request facts the edge records: `app_id`, the application the caller resolver authenticated, and on the public port `user_agent` and `remote_ip`; none of the three can be listed, and each fact is cut to 512 characters. `remote_ip` is the server's remote address, which the host takes from the gateway's `X-Forwarded-For` (`server.forward-headers-strategy` is `framework` unless the application sets it, `none` included).

properties.name: wow.http.services
properties.description: The service identities the internal port trusts by their static tokens, by service name: a call whose `Authorization: Bearer` token is one of them is that service's, which alone may send `Wow-Call`, and only to the internal port. For a deployment without CoSec; with CoSec, `wow.cosec.service.roles` names its service principals.

properties.name: wow.internal.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long a peer has to accept a connection of the cluster channel or the signal sender.

properties.name: wow.internal.dev-profiles
properties.description: The development profiles, `dev`, `local`, `test` and `demo`: in them the internal port may run without token, and `wow.backend=auto` falls back to memory when no durable backend is available.

properties.name: wow.internal.host
properties.description: The address the internal server binds, `0.0.0.0` for every interface; when not set, the host of the member address the node advertises (`wow.node.address`, else this host's address).

properties.name: wow.internal.port
properties.description: The port of the internal server, which carries the cluster channel and the wait signals; 0 for one the system chooses, which the node advertises once the server is bound.

properties.name: wow.internal.signal-queue-capacity
properties.description: The wait signals queued per origin node before they are dropped, so a slow or unreachable node cannot hold the sender's memory.

properties.name: wow.internal.token
properties.description: The service's cluster tokens, at least 32 characters each: the secret its nodes share, which alone opens the cluster channel (`/wow/internal/forward`) and the wait signals of the internal port. A node sends the first and takes any, so a token is rotated by adding the new one second, then moving it first on every node, then removing the old one; a comma-separated value (`WOW_INTERNAL_TOKEN`) is a list. A service token of `wow.http.services` opens the call routes, not these, and this token no call route. A node without one starts only in a profile of devProfiles, or with its internal port bound to the loopback interface alone, and warns: its cluster routes then take every request.

properties.name: wow.kafka.bootstrap-servers
properties.description: The brokers; the transport, the Kafka Sink and the Kafka-sourced subscriptions are wired only when it is set.

properties.name: wow.kafka.command-intake
properties.description: Whether each context the node hosts executes the commands other contexts send to its command topic, `wow.<context>.commands`. The topic must exist with as many partitions as the context's log. A context with an aggregate type routed through Kafka takes them whatever this says.

properties.name: wow.kafka.offset-gap
properties.description: What a read of another context's topic does when its partition no longer holds the offset to read from (the retention deleted it, or the topic was created again): `fail` fails the read, so the subscription stays where it is; `earliest` reads on from the earliest offset retained, and the skipped range is lost to that subscription. Either way the gap is logged as an error and counted (`wow.kafka.offset.gaps`).

properties.name: wow.kafka.poll-timeout
properties.description: The longest a consumer's poll waits; a read that is cancelled, and a partition that joins or leaves a topic's shared consumer, take effect within it.

properties.name: wow.kafka.properties
properties.description: Passed to every producer and consumer as they are (`security.protocol`, `client.id`, `linger.ms`, ...), except the settings the transport's guarantees rest on (`me.ahoo.wow.kafka.KafkaOptions`).

properties.name: wow.kafka.topic-prefix
properties.description: Put before every topic name, such as `staging.` for `staging.wow.shop.order.state`; none by default, so the topics are the Manifest's (`wow.<context>.<aggregate>.state`). The sinks write and the subscriptions read under it.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.configs
properties.description: Other topic configs `auto` creates a topic with, such as `retention.ms`.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.ddl
properties.description: How the node manages the topics its contexts own at its start: `validate` fails the start when one is missing or a command topic does not have exactly `wow.log.partitions` partitions; `auto` creates the missing ones first; `none` checks only the command topics the node reads.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.dev-profiles
properties.description: The profiles that run without durable topics, a single broker: no warning about it.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.min-insync-replicas
properties.description: The `min.insync.replicas` `auto` creates a topic with; the broker's default when not set.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.partition-refresh
properties.description: How often the node looks for partitions added to the topics it reads, and its consumers' `metadata.max.age.ms`; new partitions are read within about twice this.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.replication-factor
properties.description: The replication factor `auto` creates a topic with; the broker's default when not set.

properties.name: wow.log.append-queue.enabled
properties.description: Whether the appends of one partition are queued and committed in groups, one call a group; on when not set. A group carries more under load than single appends and costs a few per cent at low concurrency.

properties.name: wow.log.append-queue.max-batch
properties.description: The most appends one group of a partition carries; 64 when not set.

properties.name: wow.log.append-queue.merge
properties.description: Whether the groups of several partitions are merged into one call, on a log that takes several partitions a call: on by default, for MongoDB and PostgreSQL; a log that does not take them is called per partition.

properties.name: wow.log.append-queue.merge-max
properties.description: The most streams one merged call takes; 512 when not set.

properties.name: wow.log.append-queue.mergers
properties.description: The committers of the merged groups, each with one call in flight; 2 when not set.

properties.name: wow.log.handoff.capacity
properties.description: The most entries one tail holds that it has not taken; a tail further behind reads the store instead.

properties.name: wow.log.handoff.enabled
properties.description: Whether the node hands its own commits to its subscriptions' tails in memory.

properties.name: wow.log.handoff.gap-wait
properties.description: The longest a tail waits for a missing sequence that an append of the node still in flight may hold; once every such append returned without it, the tail reads the store at once.

properties.name: wow.log.max-poll-interval
properties.description: The longest a tail waits between polls that find nothing: an idle tail backs off up to it.

properties.name: wow.log.partitions
properties.description: The partitions of each context's log: fixed once the log holds entries, a power of two that divides 4096, refused at start otherwise.

properties.name: wow.log.poll-interval
properties.description: How often the tail of a PostgreSQL or MongoDB log polls while it finds entries.

properties.name: wow.log.store
properties.description: The store of every aggregate's log that `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].log.store` does not name: one of `wow.stores`, the only one when not set.

properties.name: wow.mongo.append-timeout
properties.description: How long an append's insert may take on a store that sets none in its `options.append-timeout`: below the default wait timeout, so a command appending during an outage is answered before its wait ends.

properties.name: wow.mongo.database
properties.description: The database of the log and the stores on the MongoDB backend, for a store that names none.

properties.name: wow.mongo.operation-timeout
properties.description: How long each call of a MongoDB store may take besides appends (`append-timeout`) and the schema's commands (5 minutes): a reply lost on the way fails the call instead of blocking it forever. A store's `options.operation-timeout` overrides it.

properties.name: wow.mongo.sharding
properties.description: Whether a store on a sharded cluster shards its log and snapshot collections when it creates them: `auto` when connected to a mongos with `ddl: auto`, `off` for a cluster its operators shard; a store's `options.sharding` overrides it.

properties.name: wow.node.address
properties.description: The `host:port` of this node's internal port, as the other nodes reach it.

properties.name: wow.node.id
properties.description: This node's id among the nodes of the service; a new one each start when not set.

properties.name: wow.opentelemetry.enabled
properties.description: Whether the node is traced and measured.

properties.name: wow.opentelemetry.sample-interval
properties.description: How often the gauges that are read, not heard, are sampled: the parked entries, the subscriptions' positions and a rebuild's progress.

properties.name: wow.ops.enabled
properties.description: Whether the operator's routes of the parked entries are served under `/wow/ops/parked` on the public port.

properties.name: wow.ops.publish.context
properties.description: The ops context the ledger is published to.

properties.name: wow.ops.publish.enabled
properties.description: Whether the node publishes its failure ledger to the ops context.

properties.name: wow.ops.publish.interval
properties.description: How often the node scans its ledger and publishes it; an entry is also published at once when it parks.

properties.name: wow.ops.webhook.events
properties.description: The events posted: `parked`, an entry parked, and `exhausted`, an entry spent its retries; both by default.

properties.name: wow.ops.webhook.format
properties.description: The body's format: `generic`, Wow's JSON, or `wecom`, a WeCom robot's Markdown message.

properties.name: wow.ops.webhook.headers
properties.description: The headers added to each post, such as a token the receiver checks.

properties.name: wow.ops.webhook.timeout
properties.description: How long one post may take.

properties.name: wow.ops.webhook.url
properties.description: The URL the webhook posts to; none is posted when not set.

properties.name: wow.postgres.operation-timeout
properties.description: How long each call of a PostgreSQL store may wait for a reply besides the schema's statements (5 minutes) and the queries (their own `statement_timeout`): a reply lost on the way fails the call, and its connection, instead of blocking it forever. A store's `options.operation-timeout` overrides it.

properties.name: wow.query.abac.attribute-prefix
properties.description: The prefix of the caller attributes that are ABAC tags: the attribute `abac.region` is the tag `region`.

properties.name: wow.query.abac.enabled
properties.description: Whether the queries are filtered by the caller's ABAC tags; off, nothing is restricted.

properties.name: wow.query.abac.match-missing-tag-key
properties.description: Whether a resource that lacks one of the caller's tag keys, or has it empty, matches as a public resource.

properties.name: wow.query.abac.require-principal-tags
properties.description: Whether an HTTP query whose caller has no ABAC tags is refused, instead of matching every resource; in-process queries are never refused for this.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.ceiling
properties.description: The highest bound the adaptation raises up to; not set, the provider's: PostgreSQL half a pool the appends share, or all of a `query-data-source`'s.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.connection-waits
properties.description: A period presses when at least this many callers wait for a connection of the store's pool.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.enabled
properties.description: Whether a store's query bound adapts to its write pressure.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.floor
properties.description: The lowest bound the adaptation halves down to.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.interval
properties.description: The length of one period over which the write pressure is evaluated.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.latency-factor
properties.description: A period presses when the appends' p90 latency is above this many times its baseline.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.min-latency
properties.description: The p90 append latency below which a period never presses, so the noise of fast appends is no pressure.

properties.name: wow.query.adaptive.periods
properties.description: How many pressing periods in a row halve the bound.

properties.name: wow.query.count-cache.enabled
properties.description: Whether the snapshot counts are cached.

properties.name: wow.query.count-cache.events-enabled
properties.description: Whether the events' counts are cached too; the log runs ahead of the snapshot checkpoint, so a cached events count may lag the streams for up to `ttl`.

properties.name: wow.query.count-cache.max-entries
properties.description: The most counts the cache holds.

properties.name: wow.query.count-cache.paged-totals
properties.description: Whether the totals of paged queries come from the cache too; off, each total is counted with its page, so that it agrees with its rows.

properties.name: wow.query.count-cache.ttl
properties.description: How long a count is cached at most; another node's write can make a cached count lag the rows by up to it.

properties.name: wow.query.cross-tenant.enabled
properties.description: Whether a caller that may act across scopes may query across tenants on the query routes (`Wow-Scope: tenant=*` or `tenant=("t1" "t2")`); 403 `wow.auth.forbidden` while off. A type whose tenant is fixed is still read in that tenant alone, and each such query is logged at INFO (`me.ahoo.wow.query.CrossTenantAudit`). The commands and the state reads never cross tenants.

properties.name: wow.query.dataset.config-directory
properties.description: The working directory whose `wow/dataset/` holds dataset files, `{context}.{dataset}.json`; each takes precedence over the class path's `META-INF/wow/dataset/` file of the same dataset.

properties.name: wow.query.dataset.max-concurrent
properties.description: How many dataset queries the node runs at once, so analytics queries do not overload a warehouse the Sink writes to; `0` for no bound. The bound is fixed: the warehouse's writes give the node no pressure to adapt to.

properties.name: wow.query.dataset.max-queued
properties.description: How many dataset queries may wait for a permit before the next one is refused; `wow.query.max-queued` when not set.

properties.name: wow.query.dataset.max-wait
properties.description: How long a dataset query beyond `max-concurrent` waits for a permit; `wow.query.max-wait` when not set.

properties.name: wow.query.enabled
properties.description: Whether the query routes and gateways are wired at all.

properties.name: wow.query.events.mongo-read-preference
properties.description: The MongoDB read preference of the `events` queries (`secondaryPreferred`, say), so a free filter scans a secondary rather than the primary the log appends to; the primary when not set. `wow.stores.<name>.query.read-preference` overrides it for one store.

properties.name: wow.query.events.unpinned
properties.description: Whether an `events` query that names no `aggregateId` runs: `allow` or `refuse`; refused, it is `wow.query.invalid`. `wow.stores.<name>.query.events.unpinned` and `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.unpinned` override it.

properties.name: wow.query.http.allow-exact-count
properties.description: Whether a paged query may ask for an exact total, beyond `count-limit`.

properties.name: wow.query.http.allow-expensive-operators
properties.description: Whether a query may use the expensive operators, those an index serves poorly, such as a negation or a suffix match; off also refuses a counting query without a filter.

properties.name: wow.query.http.count-limit
properties.description: The default and the largest limit of a count, and the bound of a paged query's total.

properties.name: wow.query.http.default-list-size
properties.description: The limit of a list that names none, at most `max-list-size`.

properties.name: wow.query.http.max-filter-nodes
properties.description: The most nodes a query's filter may have, the caller's scope included.

properties.name: wow.query.http.max-filter-values
properties.description: The most values one node of a query's filter may list, such as those of an `in`.

properties.name: wow.query.http.max-list-size
properties.description: The most results a list or an aggregation may ask for.

properties.name: wow.query.http.max-page-size
properties.description: The largest page of a paged or cursor query.

properties.name: wow.query.http.max-page-window
properties.description: How deep a paged query may go: the most of its page index times its page size.

properties.name: wow.query.http.max-residual-groups
properties.description: The most groups an aggregation may read when the storage cannot run its HAVING or metric sort itself and the groups are computed in the node.

properties.name: wow.query.http.timeout
properties.description: The execution timeout of every query of the entry; `0` runs without one.

properties.name: wow.query.http.unindexed-sort-expensive
properties.description: Whether a sort the storage runs without an index counts as an expensive operator, so that `allow-expensive-operators: false` refuses it too.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process-timeout
properties.description: The timeout of an in-process query that has no budget, trusted code's that dropped it (`QueryApi.trusted().unbounded()`); `0` for none.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.allow-exact-count
properties.description: Whether a paged query may ask for an exact total, beyond `count-limit`.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.allow-expensive-operators
properties.description: Whether a query may use the expensive operators, those an index serves poorly, such as a negation or a suffix match; off also refuses a counting query without a filter.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.count-limit
properties.description: The default and the largest limit of a count, and the bound of a paged query's total.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.default-list-size
properties.description: The limit of a list that names none, at most `max-list-size`.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.max-filter-nodes
properties.description: The most nodes a query's filter may have, the caller's scope included.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.max-filter-values
properties.description: The most values one node of a query's filter may list, such as those of an `in`.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.max-list-size
properties.description: The most results a list or an aggregation may ask for.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.max-page-size
properties.description: The largest page of a paged or cursor query.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.max-page-window
properties.description: How deep a paged query may go: the most of its page index times its page size.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.max-residual-groups
properties.description: The most groups an aggregation may read when the storage cannot run its HAVING or metric sort itself and the groups are computed in the node.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.timeout
properties.description: The execution timeout of every query of the entry; `0` runs without one.

properties.name: wow.query.in-process.unindexed-sort-expensive
properties.description: Whether a sort the storage runs without an index counts as an expensive operator, so that `allow-expensive-operators: false` refuses it too.

properties.name: wow.query.index.ddl
properties.description: How the snapshot backend manages the indexes of each aggregate's `x-wow-index` at startup: `auto` creates what is missing, `validate` refuses to start when one is missing, `none` does nothing.

properties.name: wow.query.max-concurrent
properties.description: How many snapshot and `events` queries each store runs at once, whichever entry asks; beyond it a query waits, then is `wow.query.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`). Not set, each store's provider derives one from its pool: PostgreSQL a quarter of a pool the appends share, at least 2, or all of a `query-data-source` of its own, 16 otherwise. `0` for no bound; `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-concurrent` overrides it for one store.

properties.name: wow.query.max-queued
properties.description: How many queries may wait for a permit before the next one is refused at once; 4 per permit when not set. `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-queued` overrides it for one store.

properties.name: wow.query.max-wait
properties.description: How long a query beyond `max-concurrent` waits in a FIFO queue for a permit before it is refused; `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-wait` overrides it for one store.

properties.name: wow.query.memory.enabled
properties.description: Whether the snapshots on a store in memory are queried, from the in-memory query backend, and the events of a log in memory scanned: for local runs, demos and tests, not for production.

properties.name: wow.query.require-authenticated-scope
properties.description: Whether an HTTP query of a built-in model is refused unless the caller's authenticated scope pins its tenant; off, a declared scope, such as a tenant header, is trusted.

properties.name: wow.query.require-explicit-entry
properties.description: Whether a query must say whether it comes over HTTP or in process; off, a query that does not say is taken as in-process.

properties.name: wow.query.sensitivity.display-comparable
properties.description: Whether filters and sorts may compare a field whose sensitivity is `DISPLAY`.

properties.name: wow.query.state.max-replay
properties.description: The most commits a state read at a version or an instant replays from the aggregate's snapshot, or from version 1; a state further away is 400 `wow.query.invalid` (`REPLAY_TOO_LONG`).

properties.name: wow.query.state.min-version-wait
properties.description: How long a read of `?minVersion=` waits for the aggregate to reach that version; past it the read is 409 `wow.query.min-version-not-reached` with the current `version`.

properties.name: wow.query.stream.chunk-size
properties.description: The records of one keyset chunk; each chunk takes a query permit.

properties.name: wow.query.stream.max-hold
properties.description: How long a stream runs before it ends with `{"reason":"hold-expired","resumable":true}`, for the client to resume it with `Last-Event-ID`; `0` for no bound.

properties.name: wow.schedules
properties.description: Per `@OnSchedule` job, by its name: `wow.schedules.<job>.*` overrides the job's rule. A job no handler of the node runs fails its start.

properties.name: wow.service
properties.description: The service's name; `spring.application.name` when not set.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.batch
properties.description: How many snapshots a rebuild rewrites per page.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.interval
properties.description: How often the snapshot maintenance runs: state revision claims, in-place rebuilds and backfill checks.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.pages
properties.description: The most pages a rebuild rewrites in one maintenance run.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.primary
properties.description: The one of the targets the write side and the queries read; the first when not set.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.store
properties.description: The context's default snapshot store, one of `wow.stores`, whose built-in subscription is `snapshot`; `wow.log.store` when not set.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.targets
properties.description: The stores every aggregate's snapshots are written to, unless its `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].snapshot.store` names others; only `wow.snapshot.store` when empty.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.write-batch
properties.description: How many snapshots of a partition the snapshot subscriptions write together at most.

properties.name: wow.standby
properties.description: Whether the node starts on standby: through the dual-run window of a migration's cut-over it serves reads of what `migrate-data` imports, refuses every command (`wow.node.standby`, 503), and handles no subscription, retries no parked entry and runs no job, until its operator resumes it on the internal port (`POST /wow/node/resume` with the cluster token, naming who resumes it). A subscription that starts at the end of its stream starts where the stream ends at the resume.

properties.name: wow.state-cache.capacity
properties.description: The aggregate states kept per context between commands; 0 keeps none. Not set (the default), each context's cache is bounded by bytes instead: a tenth of the maximum heap (`-Xmx`), split between the node's contexts, each state weighed at an estimated 1 KB plus 12 bytes per recent request it holds (its rings grow with the requests the aggregate commits, up to `recent-requests`), and at least 4096 states with full rings. Most aggregates commit few requests, so the default holds several times as many of them as a count sized for full rings. A miss costs a snapshot and a tail read before the command is decided, so the cache should hold the aggregates written often: set a capacity when states are much larger than 1 KB (a capacity times the average state size should stay well within the heap). The `wow.state-cache` counter (`hit`, `miss`, `evicted`) shows the fit.

properties.name: wow.state-cache.recent-requests
properties.description: The requests each cached aggregate keeps of those it committed last, derived from the log, so that most commands skip looking their request id up; 0 looks every request id up.

properties.name: wow.state-views.capacity
properties.description: The most state views a context keeps.

properties.name: wow.state-views.max-age
properties.description: How long a state view is kept at most.

properties.name: wow.state-views.max-bytes
properties.description: The most bytes of serialized state a context's views hold, counting two bytes a character.

properties.name: wow.stores
properties.description: The named store instances, by name: `wow.stores.<name>.type` and its settings. The aggregates whose logs are on one store form a log group, with its own partition sequences, checkpoints, parked entries and timers.

properties.name: wow.subscription.backpressure.initial-backoff
properties.description: The wait before the first retry; it doubles at each next one.

properties.name: wow.subscription.backpressure.jitter
properties.description: The share of each wait, 0 to 1, by which it is shortened at random, so that retries do not come in step.

properties.name: wow.subscription.backpressure.max-attempts
properties.description: The most attempts of an entry that meets backpressure before its aggregate parks.

properties.name: wow.subscription.backpressure.max-backoff
properties.description: The longest wait between two retries; a downstream's longer `Retry-After` still counts.

properties.name: wow.subscription.backpressure.min-concurrency
properties.description: The fewest handlings a throttled partition runs at once.

properties.name: wow.subscription.checkpoint-interval
properties.description: How often each subscription saves its checkpoint; a stop saves it too.

properties.name: wow.subscription.max-in-flight
properties.description: The entries one subscription may hold in one partition between its checkpoint and the last entry it took: it bounds both memory and what a crash replays.

properties.name: wow.subscription.parked.execution-timeout
properties.description: How long a retry may run before the partition's next owner may start another.

properties.name: wow.subscription.parked.max-retries
properties.description: The most automatic retries of a parked entry; 0 turns them off.

properties.name: wow.subscription.parked.min-backoff
properties.description: The wait before the first retry after the failure; each next one waits twice as long after the previous one started.

properties.name: wow.subscription.parked.scan-interval
properties.description: How often each node scans its subscriptions' parked entries for retries that are due.

properties.name: wow.subscription.read-retry.initial-backoff
properties.description: The wait after the first failure.

properties.name: wow.subscription.read-retry.max-attempts
properties.description: The most attempts of a call in all, the first included; for `read-retry`, the attempts after which each failure is logged as an error and retried at `max-backoff`.

properties.name: wow.subscription.read-retry.max-backoff
properties.description: The longest wait between two attempts.

properties.name: wow.subscription.read-retry.multiplier
properties.description: How many times longer each wait is than the one before; at least 1.

properties.name: wow.subscription.read-retry.timeout
properties.description: How long one attempt of a handler may run before it is cancelled and counts as failed; not set, an attempt runs as long as it takes. A read retry does not use it.

properties.name: wow.subscription.retry.initial-backoff
properties.description: The wait after the first failure.

properties.name: wow.subscription.retry.max-attempts
properties.description: The most attempts of a call in all, the first included; for `read-retry`, the attempts after which each failure is logged as an error and retried at `max-backoff`.

properties.name: wow.subscription.retry.max-backoff
properties.description: The longest wait between two attempts.

properties.name: wow.subscription.retry.multiplier
properties.description: How many times longer each wait is than the one before; at least 1.

properties.name: wow.subscription.retry.timeout
properties.description: How long one attempt of a handler may run before it is cancelled and counts as failed; not set, an attempt runs as long as it takes. A read retry does not use it.

properties.name: wow.subscription.stop-timeout
properties.description: How long a stop waits for the handlers in flight before abandoning them; an abandoned entry is handled again after the restart.

properties.name: wow.subscription.systemic.failing-aggregates
properties.description: How many different aggregates failing within `window` pause the partition; 0 turns that off.

properties.name: wow.subscription.systemic.initial-backoff
properties.description: The wait before the first probe of a paused partition; it doubles at each next one.

properties.name: wow.subscription.systemic.max-backoff
properties.description: The longest wait between two probes of a paused partition.

properties.name: wow.subscription.systemic.window
properties.description: The window in which `failing-aggregates` failures pause the partition.

properties.name: wow.subscriptions
properties.description: Per subscription, by its name (bracketed in a property name: `wow.subscriptions.[CartSaga.onOrderCreated]`).

properties.name: wow.tenant.default
properties.description: The tenant of a caller that has none, such as the anonymous one.

properties.name: wow.timers.claim-timeout
properties.description: How long the claim on a timer being sent holds: when its node dies, the next owner of the partition sends the timer again after it. Longer than a send takes.

properties.name: wow.timers.expires-after
properties.description: How late a timer may be sent, after an outage, before it is cancelled with the outcome `EXPIRED` instead; not set, every timer is sent however late.

properties.name: wow.timers.lookahead
properties.description: How far ahead each read loads the timers that fall due; a longer lookahead reads more timers at once.

properties.name: wow.timers.max-attempts
properties.description: The attempts a technical failure to send a timer gets before the timer is parked under `wow.timers`.

properties.name: wow.timers.max-early-wait
properties.description: How long a scheduled command waits in its target for its due time on the target node's clock; one that arrives earlier than that fails and is sent again later.

properties.name: wow.timers.max-fire-rate
properties.description: The most commands of timers a partition sends a second, so a backlog of overdue timers drains at that rate; not set, as fast as `parallelism` allows.

properties.name: wow.timers.parallelism
properties.description: The most commands of timers a partition sends at once.

properties.name: wow.timers.poll-interval
properties.description: How often the loop reads the timers due within `lookahead`, with one query per timer store over every partition the node owns; a timer is sent up to this late.

properties.name: wow.topics.in-memory
properties.description: Whether the node's topics are in its JVM instead of Kafka.

properties.name: wow.wait.default-timeout
properties.description: How long a command whose request names no timeout waits (`Wow-Wait-Timeout`), whichever edge it came through: at most maxTimeout.

properties.name: wow.wait.max-hops
properties.description: The most hops of a wait plan, at most WaitOptions.MAX_HOPS_CAP; each saga a chain follows adds two.

properties.name: wow.wait.max-registered
properties.description: The most waits the node holds at once, which bounds their memory: beyond it a command whose plan waits past ACCEPTED is not run and is answered `wow.command.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`), FAILED at ACCEPTED.

properties.name: wow.wait.max-timeout
properties.description: The longest wait; a longer timeout is capped to it, and a node stops within it.

properties.name: wow.wait.unknown-contexts
properties.description: Whether a wait plan may name a context the node knows no Manifest of: `allow`, checked where the chain arrives, or `reject`.
